A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, figures, and complete appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original numerical experiments on linear and polynomial systems, optimizer trajectories, and Monte Carlo evaluations of neural policies on LQR and pendulum tasks.

after.justification: v3 retains these experiments and adds policy-collapse controls, GPOMDP comparisons, Monte Carlo accuracy analyses, and MuJoCo experiments.

M1.justification: Appendix B extends the moment-evaluation framework to GPOMDP by replacing the full-trajectory return with quadratic reward-to-go terms. This is a limited procedural adaptation; the original REINFORCE estimators, Gaussian policies, and exact-moment procedures remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v3 adds Hopper-v4 and HalfCheetah-v4 locomotion experiments with MLP policies in Appendix B and Figure 10. These substantially broaden the evaluated environments beyond the retained low-dimensional control systems and pendulum task.

E2.justification: v3 adds direct REINFORCE–GPOMDP comparisons in Figure 8, empirical Monte Carlo versus exact calculations in Figure 9, and an exact-gradient Adam control for policy collapse in Figure 7. These substantially expand the comparison design beyond the retained GD, SGD, and Adam trajectory comparisons. PPO trains the new MuJoCo policies; it is not a head-to-head baseline.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include larger-batch and exact-gradient collapse controls, Monte Carlo accuracy evaluation with a ten-minute budget per iteration, and PPO experiments on MuJoCo. These are added protocols; newly listed hyperparameters for retained experiments do not establish that their settings changed.

E4.justification: Figure 7 adds controls testing whether sampling error causes collapse, together with policy log-standard-deviation and Adam-momentum diagnostics. Appendix B also tests sensitivity to the gradient estimator and the reliability of Monte Carlo variance/NSR estimates. v1 lacks these targeted analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Gradient-estimator variance is the scientific quantity studied in both versions; the added Monte Carlo accuracy comparison does not introduce a new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Figures 1–6 retain their results. New findings include delayed collapse with larger batches, no collapse in the displayed exact-gradient Adam run, lower but similarly structured GPOMDP NSR, and substantial Monte Carlo estimation errors. New MuJoCo traces are also reported, although Figure 10 labels the HalfCheetah quantity 'Variance' while its caption describes NSR.

T1.justification: New Theorem 4 and Appendix F prove a positive probability of escaping any fixed ball for a scalar SGD update under specified noise-growth and continuity assumptions. Section 5 adds baseline-residual scaling arguments and an entropy-regularized stationary-covariance formula. The original principal moment calculations and proofs are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal exact-characterization contributions remain unchanged. The introduction extends covariance/horizon scaling claims to variance as well as NSR and strengthens the motivation for exact evaluation. Its proportional initial-state-covariance wording for variance conflicts with the cubic dependence stated in Section 2.1.

C2.justification: The expanded discussion explains when exact baselines cancel small-covariance divergence, why approximation errors can preserve it, and how entropy regularization can help without guaranteeing stability. v3 also replaces the earlier universality suggestion with a narrower cross-system interpretation and explicitly leaves a general formal NSR–instability relationship open.

D1.justification: Appendix B newly supplies optimizer learning rates, batch sizes, two-layer MLPs with 64 hidden units and ReLU activations, and Monte Carlo time budgets. v1 specifies system equations and some horizons/covariances but omits most of these implementation choices. Much of this addition documents retained experiments rather than demonstrating altered implementations.

R1.justification: Appendix A expands substantially beyond its short LQR/baseline discussion to cover policy-gradient variants, tabular and partially observed settings, estimator variability, and convergence dynamics. Added comparisons with Zhao et al. (2011) and Ilyas et al. (2018), among others, clarify the relationship to prior variance-scaling results and empirical gradient deterioration.

P1.justification: The abstract, main section sequence, and most mathematical exposition remain intact. Changes include local language corrections, reorganized related work, a retitled and expanded Discussion and Conclusions section, and insertion of an Additional Experiments appendix with corresponding proof renumbering.

P2.justification: v3 adds four substantial multipanel figures: collapse controls, comparative NSR heatmaps, Monte Carlo accuracy plots, and MuJoCo trajectories. Figure 7 also redisplays original collapse curves alongside new controls and diagnostics. Existing figures are resized or relocated while retaining their results.

improvement.justification: The collapse controls and Monte Carlo accuracy study address v1's weakly tested mechanism and motivation for exact evaluation, while Appendix B supplies important missing reproducibility details. The new theorem and expanded discussion strengthen and qualify the instability argument. These are substantial gains, despite remaining uncertainty-reporting gaps and new inconsistencies in variance-scaling prose and Figure 10's labeling.
